argument_summary: The available record does not support clean model-card compliance today, but it does support a narrower certification theory if the auditor treats this as caveated rather than fully compliant. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and the public governance materials support deployment with documented limitations and ongoing risk management. The limiting fact is the current emergency-shelter-placement regression: prior approval and the informal monitoring note are contextual only, so the certification defense should be confined to a contingent packet that requires the current-release model card to expressly disclose that limitation before launch.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost evidence is admissible here beyond the general benefit of avoiding unnecessary escalation. The narrower request is therefore to avoid treating the packet as if it asserted clean compliance when the supportable position is a bounded, caveated certification theory.
claims_about_policy: Policy is best read as allowing certification when current evaluation results are reflected and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports the first half of that theory on current evaluation context and general governance practice, but not a claim that the disclosure predicate is already satisfied. Prior approval and informal monitoring can narrow risk context; they do not substitute for the required current-release disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
concessions: The current release has a documented regression on the emergency shelter placement slice that falls below the warning threshold.
No admissible evidence shows attached current-release disclosure language for that named use case.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation record or approved risk-acceptance record covering the current subgroup weakness.
The informal manual-monitoring comment is not equivalent to reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure.
The prior approval is contextual only and does not by itself substantiate the present release.
